issues.detail: Hebrew 'לֹא חָסַרְתָּ דָּבָר' means 'you have lacked nothing' (i.e., nothing was missing), but the Chinese renders '你沒有缺少什麼話' ('you have not lacked any word/speech'), adding '話' (word/speech) which is not in the Hebrew. The Hebrew 'דָּבָר' here means 'thing' in the sense of 'anything', not 'word/speech' in this context. This changes the meaning from lacking nothing at all to lacking no word.
